recipes.name: Spicy Chipotle Turkey Burgers
ingredients_raw: 1 chipotle chile in adobo sauce, finely chopped

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat, and lightly oil grate. Place the ground turkey, onion, cilantro, chipotle chile pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, seasoned salt, and black pepper in a mixing bowl; mix well. Form into 4 patties.

Cook the hamburgers on the preheated grill until the turkey is no longer pink in the center, about 4 minutes per side. Place the mozzarella slices on the patties 2 minutes before they are ready. Serve on the toasted buns.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Chipotle Turkey Burgers
raw_recipe.description: With a chipotle chile pepper, mozzarella cheese and other seasonings, you will absolutely love this spicy, yet flavorful, burger!

video.description: In this video you'll see how simple it is to jazz up turkey patties. The kick of heat comes from chipotle peppers which you can adjust to your liking. After a smoky trip to the grill, these burgers are topped with mozzarella cheese, and are especially delicious garnished with fresh avocado slices.

review.reviewBody: Wish I could give this one more than 5 stars... These were the best turkey burgers I've yet to make! I did use 2 chipotle peppers because we like our food spicy, and they came out just right. I was afraid that using 2 of them would overpower the meat, but it did not. Now here's a GREAT tip to keeping these tasty burgers moist: instead of adding a slice of mozzarella on top, make 8 thin patties instead of 4 thick ones. Put a heaping tablespoon of finely shredded mozzarella on the center of 4 of them and then top each with the other thin patty. Then just seal up the sides of the burger. That way, when you bite into one of these yummy delights, the cheese will ooze out of the middle. Even my husband enjoyed these, (he ate 2 of them!), and he NEVER has been impressed with any type of turkey burger! Thanks for submitting this one; I'll be making it again for sure!

Wow, we LOVED these burgers. Used ground chicken (didn't have turkey) and only change was to add 2 tbsp dried bread crumbs since the mix was too moist to form into burgers without the crumbs. The burgers reached 160 in 6 minutes on our grill "oiled to prevent sticking) at about 350 degrees. . Unbelievable delicious! Great taste and texture, moist and flavorful! Served with Pepper Jack cheese, purple onion, and mustard; and grilled herbed sliced potatoes and grilled zucchini chucks.

I thought these burgers had great flavor and very juicy. I mixed them up and let the flavors meld together in the fridge for 4-5 hours before I made the patties. Ground turkey is easier to work with when it is cold. I used my George Foreman grill to cook them and it took 8 minutes. They had a nice char on both sides. I will be making these again!

I don't care much for turkey but will go out of my way to make this. Instead of cheese I serve it on a pretzel bun with homemade mayo on one half and Major Grey's chutney on the other. Delicious and great to broil if you don't want to grill, and freeze the patties for a treat when you're too tired to cook. I can't imagine anyone not liking these and of course you can customize the toppings and add-ins to your liking. A great , easy recipe!

We quadrupled the recipe and used 6 peppers. They were So delicious! I ate the last one two days later and I think it was even better, so I think next time I'll mix it all together a couple hours before cooking. We also mixed a little of the sauce from the chipotles with some mayo for a little extra kick. Can't wait to make these again!

Awesome burger! Lighter and tastier than beef. I like the flavor of onion but not the texture so I grated mine and it was perfect. I also puréed the chipotle pepper and adobo sauce and used 2 heaping tablespoons in the recipe and froze the rest. I pan fried instead of grilling because the mixture was a little loose. Came out great. Burger was very juicy and flavorful.

HOLY COW!!!...or should I say holy turkey?Thank you for sharing this incredible recipe. I am a chef and I made this for my fiancé. He said this was one of the best meals I’ve made and definitely the best burger I’ve made. I adjusted it a bit according to our tastes as we all have opinionated and particular taste buds. Sautéed the chopped onions until translucent and added 1/2 tablespoon of minced garlic. Also added 3 tablespoons of mayo (I do this with all my burger meat to maintain moisture), 4 minced strips of bacon, added an extra chipotle, doubled the garlic powder (can you tell that we love garlic?), filled the middle of the burgers with marinated mozzarella, and topped them with pepper-jack cheese and Yum-Yum sauce. Obviously if you’re doing turkey burgers to be healthy these modifications aren’t for you lol. I want to give a major shoutout to the creator of this recipe. You are much appreciated ??

I doubled the chipotle peppers, but I did remove the seeds. I browned in a pan and baked them in the oven. These are very flavourful. Didn't use the cheese or buns, just had on their own. I have made twice and it's a keeper!

This was a really good meal that was easy and pretty forgiving. I say forgiving because after I mixed all the ingredients together my wife called and had invited more friends over for dinner. I added more turkey and eyeballed the seasonings. I cooked them on my Yoder YS460 smoker at 350 for about 15 minutes to an internal temp of 180. Everyone left the table full and kept on giving me compliments throughout the rest of the night.

OMG was this good! Far exceeded my expectations. I didn't have the chile but found a substitute that worked perfectly. [Sub: 1 chipotle with adobo = 1 T. tomato sauce, 1 T. cider vinegar, 1 t. powdered chipotle chile pepper, 1/2 t. cumin and a pinch of oregano, salt and pepper] We found the burgers to be a tad spicy so will likely skip the black pepper in both the substitute and main recipe in the future, and possibly cut back on the powdered chipotle also. Excellent recipe!

These turkey burgers were amazing! I read the reviews prior to making them and followed the advise of putting cheese in the middle. I followed the directions exactly otherwise. I made a Chipotle mayo and put it on a brioche bun with avocado and topped the burgers with pepper jack cheese. My husband took one bite and said, “wow these are good.”

These are truly the best spicy turkey burgers we’ve ever had. We’ve been making this recipe for years and it’s always on our rotation. I have some friends, family that insisted they don’t like turkey burgers, and they love these! Great recipe.
Excellent recipe

I made half the recipe. I didn’t have the chile In adobo so I followed another viewer’s suggestion and used 1 tsp of smoked paprika. I also have to watch my sodium so I didn’t use seasoned salt or chile powder, but honestly, after adding a tad of stone ground mustard, mozzarella, tomato, avocado, and sliced onion - I didn’t miss it!
This recipe has so much flavor. It takes ground turkey and makes a great burger. I never tire of it.

These are great and we made them often. As some others have said, if my store is out of the adobo chilis and I don't want to make another stop, I'll substitute 4oz of green chilis (hot or mild, whatever) and these still turn out fantastic.

I didn’t have chipotle peppers so I used 2tsp of smoked paprika. I also added a small 4 oz can of mild green chilis which added great moisture! Then I grilled them and topped them with a sprinkle of grated sharp cheddar. (I didn’t have any mozzarella) served with corn bread and beans and rice! My whole family agreed this recipe is definitely a keeper!! It was so yummy!
Cilantro was a little strong, we'll cut back on it next time, otherwise the burgers were great!

I made them exactly as stated except that we topped a couple of the burgers with Monterey Jack cheese. Both versions were equally good. We topped them with Mayo, sliced avocado, and thinly sliced red onion.
Awesome recipe! I made it as is and loved that it didn't call for eggs or breadcrumbs. This will remain a house staple!
